content.body:
The Douglas-built Havoc I was a very effective intruder/attack aircraft. This sturdy and high-performance airframe continued to evolve through the war as the A-20, and eventually into the A-26 Invader, perhaps the ultimate expression of the attack/intruder style bomber as it evolved during the war years.
Used by France, Britain, Russia, and the USAAF in almost every theater of war during the 1940s, the A-20 was truly a legendary attack aircraft. While the early models such as the ones in Battleground Europe at present were only armed with four pilot controlled rifle caliber machine guns and one defensive dorsal gunner ... later on these would wind up being multiple (up to 8 or 10) .50 caliber heavy machine guns or four 20mm cannons.
British Havoc Is were the first aircraft used by USAAF aircrews against German targets in WWII during the early famous low altitude "rodeo" raids staged against airfield targets in now German held French coastal territory.
